passage:
A large tree in the city square was said to be older than the city hall. It had survived storms, road changes, and nearby construction.
When engineers planned a new underground parking lot, the tree's roots became a problem. Some wanted to remove the tree. Others wanted to change the plan.
The city held public meetings. Finally, engineers redesigned part of the project to protect the roots. It cost more, but many residents supported the decision.
The tree was not famous like a statue, but it had watched generations pass.
A living landmark can be harder to protect than stone, yet it may mean just as much to a community.
